title: Diesel training and discrimination in civilian jobs
summary: Back home he could not work as a diesel mechanic because Negroes were not allowed, and he got a movie projector job when someone died.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: Well, when you learned something about diesels, did that help you with your mechanical law?

Neither one of them did help me because when I came back here, movement, had a gang of movement pitching machines operating at that time and I applied for a job and couldn't get a job nowhere. The man told me to put my name on the roster as a move projector operator. And I had to wiggle my name and somebody died for me to get a job as a move projector operator. Diesel mechanic, they wasn't allowing Negroes to operate at that time. Not diesel. But today you can do it. You can drive anything you want.
But that was to operate a diesel truck?
Yeah. I played all that. Ton of food, carry-offs, creepers, D4, D8, D12, I drove all that.
But you couldn't do it in civilian life?
Did you do some of that in the Army?
